source_refs.note: 3. B Cells: a main subheading of 21.3.1 Components of the Immune System, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 176-177.

blocks.text: The B cells also develop in bone marrow but unlike T cells, they do not travel to the thymus for maturity. They complete their maturation in the bone marrow. From there they are released to circulate in the bloodstream and lymph. Individual B cells, like T cells, are specialized to recognize particular antigens. When a B cell encounters an antigen, it begins to divide into many new cells called plasma cells. Each plasma cell produces an antibody that sticks to the antigen, marking it for destruction.
